b_dali_1.first_mention_attestation: Founded as the Dali Kingdom and capital name in 937 CE by Duan Siping (recorded in Xin Wudaishi and Songshi, Vol. 488), succeeding the Nanzhao capital of Yangjumie City.
b_dali_1.etymology_analysis: Dali (大理) is a Chinese dynastic and capital name adopted by Duan Siping in 937 CE when he established the Kingdom of Dali at Yangjumie City, signifying 'great governance' or 'great order.'

older_name_by_867.notes: The Erhai basin was established as Yeyu County in 109 BCE, became Nanzhao's Taihe City in 739 CE and Yangjumie City in 779 CE, and was renamed Dali in 937 CE.

b_ningbei.first_mention_attestation: Established as Ningbei Jiedu (宁北节度) by Nanzhao in 794 CE (10th year of Zhenyuan), with its seat at Ningbei City recorded in Xin Tangshu (Vol. 222a) and Manshu (Vol. 6).
b_ningbei.etymology_analysis: Ningbei (宁北) is a Nanzhao-era Chinese administrative name meaning 'pacifying the north,' designating the northern frontier commandery on the eastern border of former Han Yeyu County.

b_yunnan.first_mention_attestation: Established in 109 BCE (2nd year of Yuanfeng, Western Han) as Yunnan County under Yizhou Commandery, recorded in Hanshu (Vol. 28a) and later as Tang Yunnan Zhou / Yunnan City in Manshu (Vol. 6).
b_yunnan.etymology_analysis: Yunnan (云南, 'south of the clouds') was first attested as a Han county name in 109 BCE at modern Xiangyun (Yunnan驿), later giving its name to the Tang commandery and the province.

b_bipan.first_mention_attestation: Recorded as the Bipan/Mipan tribe (閟畔部), one of the thirty-seven tribes of the Dali Kingdom that submitted to the Mongols in the 13th century (recorded in Yuanshi, Vol. 61).

b_lulu.first_mention_attestation: Attested in Tang-era records Manshu (863 CE) and Xin Tangshu (Vol. 222b) as the Lulu Man (卢鹿蛮 / 盧鹿蠻), one of the seven Dongcuan Wu-man tribes allied with Nanzhao.

b_nongdong.first_mention_attestation: Established in 109 BCE (2nd year of Yuanfeng, Western Han) as Nongdong County under Yizhou Commandery, recorded in Hanshu (Vol. 28a), and later Nanzhao's Nongdong City in Manshu (Vol. 6).

b_yunlong.first_mention_attestation: Recorded as Yunlong Dian Military and Civilian Prefecture (云龙甸军民府) in Yuanshi (Vol. 61, compiled 1370 CE), named for the morning clouds rising like a dragon over the Lancang River.

b_kunmimg.first_mention_attestation: Established in 619 CE (2nd year of Wude, Tang dynasty) as Kunming County under Xizhou (modern Yanyuan County, Sichuan), recorded in Xin Tangshu (Vol. 42) and Manshu (Vol. 6).

b_miangu.first_mention_attestation: Renamed Miangu County (绵谷县) in 598 CE (18th year of Kaihuang, Sui dynasty) from Xing'an County as the seat of Lizhou, recorded in Suishu (Vol. 29) and Jiu Tangshu (Vol. 39).

b_jinggu.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Jinggu County (景谷县) from the Sui dynasty (Suishu, Vol. 29, Yicheng Commandery) and Tang dynasty (Xin Tangshu, Vol. 40, Lizhou).

b_jiameng.first_mention_attestation: Established as Jiameng County (葭萌县) in the Qin dynasty (314 BCE) / Western Han, recorded in Shiji, Hanshu (Geography Treatise), and Xin Tangshu (Vol. 40).

b_fuyu.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Fuyu County (伏虞县) from the Southern Liang dynasty (502–557 CE) and in Suishu (Vol. 29) and Xin Tangshu (Vol. 40) under Pengzhou.

b_tongchang.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Tongchang County (同昌县) from the Western Wei / Northern Zhou period (c. 553–581 CE) and in Suishu (Vol. 29) and Xin Tangshu (Vol. 40) under Fuzhou.

b_baishi.first_mention_attestation: Established as Baishi County (白石县) in the Western Wei Feidi period (c. 553 CE) under Dongba Prefecture (later Jizhou), recorded in Suishu (Vol. 29) and Xin Tangshu (Vol. 40).

b_sanquan.first_mention_attestation: Established as Sanquan County (三泉县) in 621 CE (4th year of Wude, Tang dynasty) by splitting Miangu County as the seat of Nan'an Prefecture, recorded in Xin Tangshu (Vol. 40).

b_xixiang.first_mention_attestation: Renamed Xixiang County (西乡县) in 281 CE (2nd year of Taikang, Western Jin dynasty) from Nanxiang County, recorded in Jinshu (Geography Treatise) and Xin Tangshu (Vol. 40).
